Why IT Services Hungary Are So Appealing to Many Companies?

The Hungarian IT market’s compound annual growth rate (CAGR) is estimated to reach 8.60% during 2023-2028. For comparison, analysts expect the US CAGR for the same period to be 6.70%. Researchers forecast that the Hungarian IT sector will generate $1.57b in 2023, while Hungary IT outsourcing will dominate with its sales of $0.56b. 

Hungary’s tech export value grew steadily from $14.5b in 2015 to $19.67 in 2021. The number of ICT (Information and Communication) employees increased from 71,902 in 2010 to 100,409 in 2020. And as of July 2023, the quantity of Hungary-based IT companies registered on LinkedIn is around 5,600. 

The statistics prove that the demand for Hungarian IT professionals is growing, and PHP, Lua, .NET, Python, and Java are the most popular programming languages in the country. And apart from the lower Hungary developer rates, there are several reasons these specialists are so popular:

  • Hungary is an EU member. Labor laws in Hungary comply with European standards. This makes Hungary nearshoring simple for Europe-based companies. Also, US businesses find cooperation with engineers from an EU member country more reliable. 
  • Hungary has a comfortable time zone. Located in Central Europe, Hungary has no time difference from Germany, Switzerland, the Netherlands, etc. So nearshoring Budapest tech experts for Western European countries offers 100% of shared business hours. 
  • Hungary is financially stable. The financial stability report as of May 2023 claims that the Hungarian banking system is robust. The capital and liquidity of the country’s banks are strong, while economic stability risks are limited.
  • Hungary boasts a high level of tech education. 11 tech universities in Hungary got into the Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2023. This list rates 1,799 universities in 104 countries. Among them are the universities of Budapest, Lorand, Debrecen, Obuda, Pecs, Szeged, and Miskolc. 
  • Hungarians have good English skills. The EF English Proficiency Index report tests around 2.1 million adults in 111 countries/regions. And in 2022, Hungary was ranked 18 and got the “high proficiency” status. This means most technicians speak English fluently.

  • Szeged. 1,800 software developers marked the third largest city in Hungary as their place of work. Each month a Java developer Szeged or other Szeged-based programmers earn about $2,769. 
  • Miskolc. Miskolc is the fourth largest Hungarian city located in the country’s north. 482 software developers are based in Miskolc, according to LinkedIn. The average remuneration of an engineer there is $2,778 per month.
  • Pecs. The fifth largest city is in the south of Hungary, and 563 programming specialists mark it as their place of living. $2,195 is the average monthly salary a software developer can get in Pecs.
